idea-plugin.name: TestInsanity
idea-plugin.description:
Keep tests and the code they test in sync.

Rename a subject and its tests follow. Rename a test and its subject follows. Jump between the two, and see in the gutter which methods have a test and which do not.

TestInsanity reads your convention from a pattern instead of guessing at it:

  ${className}Test   maps Color to ColorTest
  (test|)${subjectName}*   maps isDarkColor() to testIsDarkColor_whenBlack()

Several patterns can be active at once, separated by ;, so ${className}Test, ${className}IT and ${className}Spec coexist in one project.

What it does
  • Renaming, both ways — subject class to test classes, test class to subject, subject method to test methods, test method to subject. Proposed renames appear in the standard Rename related items dialog, so you can deselect any of them.
  • Navigation — Go To -> Jump to Sibling (CTRL+ALT+`) moves between a method and its test method, not only between their classes. Navigate -> Test (CTRL+SHIFT+T) and Create Test follow the same scheme.
  • Gutter icons — the sibling class or method, its JUnit 5 DisplayName when it has one, and a distinct icon for a test with no subject.
  • Create what is missing — Alt+Enter on a subject creates the test class in the module test source root, or the test method carrying the right framework annotation (Java sources).
  • Configuration in version control — a .testinsanity.json at the project root pins the scheme for everyone, the way .editorconfig does, so nothing needs to live in .idea. Whatever the file leaves out stays a personal preference.
Built for real projects
  • JUnit 4, JUnit 5 — including nested and parameterized tests — and TestNG
  • Java and Kotlin; Kotlin support is optional, and the plugin works without it
  • Kotlin backtick test names, since patterns accept spaces
  • Tests in a module of their own, resolved in both directions
  • Abstract or inherited test classes
Everything is configured per project under Settings -> Tools -> TestInsanity. Refactoring support toggles from the Tools menu, gutter icons from Settings -> Editor -> General -> Gutter Icons.

Please report issues:
https://github.com/bitstrings/testinsanity/issues

Pino Silvaggio
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v2.0.0

New
  • Project configuration in .testinsanity.json at the project root, so the naming scheme lives in version control instead of in .idea. Keys the file declares win over the IDE settings and appear disabled in the settings dialog; keys it omits stay personal. The file is re-read whenever it changes, including on branch switches.
  • Renaming works in all four directions: subject class to test classes, test class to subject class, subject method to test methods, and test method to subject method.
  • Renaming goes through the standard Rename related items dialog, so it also applies to in-place rename and lets you deselect any proposed rename.
  • Several alternative patterns per project, separated by ; and tried in order, so Test, Tests, IT and Spec can coexist.
  • Navigate -> Test (CTRL+SHIFT+T) and Create Test follow the configured naming scheme.
  • New intention (Alt+Enter): create the missing test class or test method for the subject.
  • JUnit 5 nested test classes are matched.
  • Patterns accept spaces, for Kotlin backtick test names, with a matching preset.
  • Optional @DisplayName generation and rename synchronization.
  • Gutter icons are computed off the highlighting pass and cached, appear in every JVM language, and can be switched off in Settings -> Editor -> General -> Gutter Icons.
Fixed
  • Renaming a subject class did not rename its test classes.
  • Renaming a test class or a test method did not rename its subject.
  • A test living in its own module never resolved its subject.
  • Which sibling was picked followed index order and could differ between runs.
  • A test method was counted twice when two matching test classes were related by inheritance.
  • A nested helper class inside a test class was reported as a test of the outer subject.
  • The settings Apply button ignored changes to the renaming checkbox.
  • A damaged TestInsanity.xml could leave the plugin inert.
Changed
  • Show renaming dialog is now Pre-select test renames: the dialog is the platform Rename related items dialog, and this setting decides whether the proposed renames start checked.

v1.3.0
  • 2026.1+
  • Kotlin K2 mode support.
  • Kotlin support is now optional: the plugin works without the Kotlin plugin.
  • Jump to Sibling now falls back to the class when a Kotlin function has no matching JVM method.
  • Fixed errors when renaming Kotlin functions that have no matching JVM method.
